name: round

name: floor
blurb: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical floor. E.g. 3.7 replaced with to 3, and -4.2 replaced with -5.

name: ceil
blurb: Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to their mathematical ceiling. E.g. 3.2 replaced with 4, and -4.2 replaced with -4.

name: toBipolar

name: fromBipolar

name: range

name: rangex

name: range2

name: bite
blurb: Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers. Similar to slice, but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

name: linger
blurb: Selects the given fraction of the pattern and repeats that part to fill the remainder of the cycle.

name: swingBy
blurb: The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if x is 0 it does nothing, 0.5 delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

name: swing
blurb: Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

name: when

name: off
blurb: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

name: brak
blurb: Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of breakbeat feel.

name: rev
blurb: Reverse all haps in a pattern

name: pressBy
blurb: Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

name: press
blurb: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

name: palindrome
blurb: Applies rev to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

name: pace

name: shrink
blurb: Experimental Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times. A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: grow
blurb: Experimental Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :), that number of times. A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: chop
blurb: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'. It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.

name: splice

name: squiz

It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

name: Pattern
blurb: Create a pattern. As an end user, you will most likely not create a Pattern directly.

blurb: Returns a new pattern, with the function applied to the value of each hap. It has the alias fmap.

params.name: func
params.doc: to to apply to the value

name: fmap
blurb: see withValue

name: appWhole
blurb: Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that pattern of functions.

name: appBoth
blurb: When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps with those in the given pattern of values. A new pattern is returned, with each matching value applied to the corresponding function. In this _appBoth variant, where timespans of the function and value haps are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

name: appLeft
blurb: As with appBoth, but the whole timespan is not the intersection, but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets, are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left hand or inner pattern).

name: appRight
blurb: As with appLeft, but whole timespans are instead taken from the pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer pattern.

name: queryArc
blurb: Query haps inside the given time span.

name: splitQueries
blurb: Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to happen within a cycle.

name: withQuerySpan
blurb: Returns a new pattern, where the given function is applied to the query timespan before passing it to the original pattern.

name: withQueryTime
blurb: As with withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the query timespan.

name: withHapSpan
blurb: Similar to withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to the timespans of all haps returned by pattern queries (both part timespans, and where present, whole timespans).

name: withHapTime
blurb: As with withHapSpan, but the function is applied to both the begin and end time of the hap timespans.

name: withHaps
blurb: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the list of haps returned by every query.

name: withHap
blurb: As with withHaps, but applies the function to every hap, rather than every list of haps.

name: setContext
blurb: Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

name: withContext

name: stripContext

name: withLoc

name: filterHaps

name: filterValues
blurb: As with filterHaps, but the function is applied to values inside haps.

name: removeUndefineds

name: onsetsOnly

name: discreteOnly

name: defragmentHaps

name: firstCycle

blurb: Experimental Aligns the steps of the patterns, creating polymeters. The patterns are repeated until they all fit the cycle. For example, in the below the first pattern is repeated twice, and the second is repeated three times, to fit the lowest common multiple of six steps.
example:
// The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")
polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

example:
// The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")
polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

name: stepcat
blurb: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle. The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair. Has the alias timecat.

name: timeCat
blurb: 'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle. The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair. Has the alias timecat.

name: timecat
blurb: Aliases for stepcat

name: stepalt
blurb: Experimental Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'. Similar to stepcat, but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.
example:
stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()
// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()

name: take
blurb: Experimental Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest). A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.
example:
"bd cp ht mt".take("2").sound()
// The same as "bd cp".sound()

name: drop
blurb: Experimental Drops the given number of steps from a pattern. A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: extend
blurb: Experimental extend is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count accordingly. So stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".
example:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

name: expand
blurb: Experimental Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

name: contract
blurb: Experimental Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also expand.

name: tour
blurb: Experimental Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
example:
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

name: zip
blurb: Experimental 'zips' together the steps of the provided patterns. This can create a long repetition, taking place over a single, dense cycle. Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
example:
zip("e f", "e f g", "g [f e] a f4 c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

name: voicing
blurb: Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params: chord: Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7 dict: voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary anchor: the note that is used to align the chord mode: how the voicing is aligned to the anchor below: top note <= anchor duck: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded above: bottom note >= anchor offset: whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing n: if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved All of the above controls are optional, except chord. If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.

name: fscope
signature: fscope(color: string, scale: number, pos: number, lean: number, min: number, max: number)
blurb: Renders an oscilloscope for the frequency domain of the audio signal.

params.name: color
params.doc: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.doc: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

params.name: lean
params.doc: y-axis alignment where 0 = top and 1 = bottom

name: scope
signature: scope(config: object, align: boolean, color: string, thickness: number, scale: number, pos: number, trigger: number)
blurb: Renders an oscilloscope for the time domain of the audio signal.

params.name: align
params.doc: if 1, the scope will be aligned to the first zero crossing. defaults to 1

params.name: color
params.doc: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.doc: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

params.name: trigger
params.doc: amplitude value that is used to align the scope. defaults to 0.

name: tscope
signature: scope(config: object, align: boolean, color: string, thickness: number, scale: number, pos: number, trigger: number)
blurb: Renders an oscilloscope for the time domain of the audio signal.

name: spectrum
signature: spectrum(config: object, thickness: integer, speed: integer, min: integer, max: integer)
blurb: Renders a spectrum analyzer for the incoming audio signal.
